q1_issues.issue: the subject `good` is a substantivized adjective (a property/abstract quality, not an individual), so `Member` puts a property in the individual slot against the Member-vs-Inheritance discipline, which routes kinds and properties to `Inheritance` on both sides.
the stated relation is enemy-of, but it is recorded only as the generic opaque `Possession` link, so which relation holds between good and great is lost (the atom reads as great possessing good).

q2_gaps: substantivized adjectives used as abstract entity arguments ('good', 'great') — the instruction set picks Member vs Inheritance by individual-vs-kind and never says which an abstract quality counts as

equative 'X is the N of Y' where the predicate nominal is definite and takes its own of-complement — no witness is minted for the predicate noun, so there is no symbol for the argument PP to attach to and the complement lands on the subject instead
notes: The kind-level 0.9 confidence is right per the definitional-vs-empirical dial. A `Symmetric`-tagged relation ((Enemy good great) + (Symmetric Enemy)) is the one open-class relation the instruction set licenses and would have kept the relation name, but only if enemy-of is read as mutual by meaning, which this aphorism arguably is not.
